blindSummary:
This state/province is the most consistent lethal hotspot for transgender people (including locally recognised trans-feminine identities) within the country's most affected region: 11 killings in 2024 (3rd-highest national total, 1st within the region) and 8 in 2025 (tied for the highest state total in the country). Against a population of ~9 million this yields roughly 0.9 killings per million per year - more than double the national rate of ~0.38 per million. A 2025 monitoring report also notes a concentration of black victims among this state's killings.

This places the state/province modestly below the country-wide baseline. The deviation is driven by sustained, patterned lethal exposure rather than any legal distinction - the federal constitution and penal code apply uniformly across the country. Compared with a far more populous peer state/province (~21 million people) that matched this state's absolute 2025 count of 8 killings, the larger state's per-capita rate sits at the national average, making this state/province the higher-risk one on a rate basis.

For a visibly trans visitor, the pattern matters: the killings are concentrated on young black trans women in public space - precisely the exposure profile of a conspicuous traveller - and the consistency across two years signals an entrenched environment rather than a statistical blip.
